transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. As we all know, we're here to discuss the six-week pilot to reduce classroom disruptions caused by student cell-phone use. The draft proposal currently covers grades 9 and 10, suggests placing phones in open classroom bins, and lists September 2, 2026 as the tentative launch date. Before I can approve the pilot's final scope, procedures, and launch record, we need to follow our agenda and hear reports from our participating teacher, our counselor, and our technology coordinator. Who would like to begin?

transcript.text: I'd like to begin with my report. In my classroom trial across all 9th-grade sections, I recorded 23 phone-related interruptions in just two weeks. However, when I tested numbered locking pouches, interruptions were significantly reduced. Based on those results, I recommended in my team notes a grade-9-only pilot using one pouch per student. I should note that those team notes have not yet been added to the draft proposal.

transcript.text: Two students have active safety plans requiring them to receive time-sensitive messages from their caregivers during the school day. I confirmed the plans with both families this week, but the exception has not yet been entered in the pilot procedure. This means whatever approach we approve—whether open bins or locking pouches—must include a documented exception process so these students can access time-sensitive communications from their caregivers.
